claims.text: The plugin fetches the signal via GET {PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL}/v1/signal/:wallet, defaulting to https://api.predge.io.
claims.quote: GET {PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL}/v1/signal/:wallet (default `https://api.predge.io`, free, unauthenticated) through `safeFetch`
claims.reasoning: DEFAULT_PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL is set to https://api.predge.io; resolveBaseUrl falls back to it when PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL is unset; fetchSignedSignal constructs the URL as /v1/signal/{wallet} and calls safeFetch with method GET.

claims.text: Every outbound request passes through assertUrlIsPublic as an always-on SSRF check.
claims.quote: behind an always-on `assertUrlIsPublic` SSRF check
claims.reasoning: The testPredge function in test.ts makes an outbound request using raw fetch() without calling assertUrlIsPublic, contradicting the claim that every outbound request passes through this SSRF check.

checked: plugins/predge/steps/read-signal.ts (delegates to fetchSignedSignal, no direct outbound request)
plugins/predge/test.ts:31 (testPredge — calls raw fetch() directly with no assertUrlIsPublic check)
tests/unit/predge-read-signal.test.ts (mocks assertUrlIsPublic, not a production code path)

claims.text: The fetch uses a 10-second AbortSignal.timeout.
claims.quote: with a 10s `AbortSignal.timeout`
claims.reasoning: FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS is defined as 10_000 ms; AbortSignal.timeout(FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS) is passed as the signal parameter to safeFetch.

claims.text: The response body is capped at 64 KiB, checked against content-length before the body is read.
claims.quote: a 64 KiB cap on the body, checked against `content-length` before it is read
claims.reasoning: MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES = 64 * 1024; the content-length header is read and compared before response.text() is called, so an oversized declared body is rejected before it is materialised.
claims.maintainer: the 64 KiB cap checked by header and then by length

claims.text: The response body is also checked against the body length before it is parsed.
claims.quote: against the body length before it is parsed
claims.reasoning: After response.text(), body.length is compared against MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES before JSON.parse(body), so the body length is checked before parsing.
claims.maintainer: the 64 KiB cap checked by header and then by length

claims.text: Attestation verification runs six ordered checks: scheme, signer, ed25519 signature, subject binding, resource binding, and freshness.
claims.quote: Six ordered checks: scheme; signer pinned to Predge's published key … ed25519 signature over the canonical payload; subject binding … resource binding … and freshness
claims.reasoning: verifyPredgeSignal performs exactly six sequential checks: scheme, signer, ed25519 signature, subject binding, resource binding, and freshness, each gated by a return-on-fail.
claims.maintainer: six ordered checks with resource fifth

claims.text: The signer is pinned to Predge's published key; the default pin is a source constant and PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID can override it.
claims.quote: signer pinned to Predge's published key (default is a source constant, `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` overrides it, and the key the response carries is never trusted on its own)
claims.reasoning: DEFAULT_PINNED_SIGNER is a source constant; the pinned value is resolved as (input.expectedKeyId || DEFAULT_PINNED_SIGNER); read-signal.ts passes credentials.PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID as expectedKeyId.

claims.text: The key the response carries is never trusted on its own.
claims.quote: the key the response carries is never trusted on its own
claims.reasoning: signer = raw.keyId is extracted but compared against the pinned constant rather than accepted directly; verification fails if they do not match.

claims.text: Subject binding checks the attestation subject against the requested wallet.
claims.quote: subject binding to the requested wallet
claims.reasoning: walletInPayload = raw.payload.wallet; subjectMatch = normalizeWallet(walletInPayload) === normalizeWallet(requestedWallet); fails with 'signal is about a different wallet' on mismatch.

claims.text: Resource binding compares the signed resource field against conviction:<wallet>, so a different signed product about the same wallet under the same key is not accepted as a conviction signal.
claims.quote: `resource` binding to `conviction:<wallet>`, so a different signed product about the same wallet under the same key is not read as a conviction signal
claims.reasoning: RESOURCE_PREFIX = 'conviction:'; expectedResource is built as conviction:<requestedWallet>; raw.resource is compared against it and fails if mismatched, blocking foreign signed products.

claims.text: Freshness is checked: issuedAt must be within the max-age window (default 600 s, configurable via PREDGE_MAX_SIGNAL_AGE_SECONDS) with one minute of skew tolerance.
claims.quote: freshness (`issuedAt` within a max-age window, default 600s, `PREDGE_MAX_SIGNAL_AGE_SECONDS` to tune, one minute of skew tolerance)
claims.reasoning: DEFAULT_MAX_SIGNAL_AGE_SECONDS = 600, MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS = 60_000; maxAgeSeconds is read from PREDGE_MAX_SIGNAL_AGE_SECONDS; ageMs is checked against both bounds.

claims.text: conviction is checked to be a finite number in the range 0–100; a numeric string such as "99999" is a failure, not a valid value.
claims.quote: `conviction` a finite number in 0-100 (a numeric string is a failure, not a number — `"99999" >= 80` coerces true in a template gate)
claims.reasoning: parseConvictionPayload checks typeof conviction !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(conviction), which rejects the string '99999' at the typeof check, then enforces the 0–100 range.
claims.maintainer: the shape gate with no coercion

claims.text: action is checked to be one of accumulate, reduce, or hold.
claims.quote: `action` one of `accumulate`/`reduce`/`hold`
claims.reasoning: PREDGE_ACTIONS = ['accumulate','reduce','hold']; parseConvictionPayload checks PREDGE_ACTIONS.includes(raw.action) and fails with a descriptive reason if it is not one of those three.
claims.maintainer: the shape gate with no coercion

claims.text: window is checked to be one of 7d or 30d.
claims.quote: `window` one of `7d`/`30d`
claims.reasoning: PREDGE_WINDOWS = ['7d','30d']; parseConvictionPayload checks PREDGE_WINDOWS.includes(raw.window) and fails if the value is not in that set.
claims.maintainer: the shape gate with no coercion

claims.text: All three payload fields (conviction, action, window) are required; nothing is coerced.
claims.quote: each required. Nothing is coerced.
claims.reasoning: All three fields are validated with strict type checks (no Number(), String() coercion); absent fields cause the typeof or includes checks to fail, making each field implicitly required.
claims.maintainer: the shape gate with no coercion

claims.text: The step fails on either the verification gate or the payload-shape gate, including the reason or the field with its received and expected types in the error.
claims.quote: The step fails on either gate, with the reason, or the field and its received and expected types, in its error
claims.reasoning: Verification failure returns error with verification.reason; payload-shape failure returns error with parsed.reason built by describeValue() which includes the received type and value for each field.

claims.text: There is no verified flag in the success output; the step cannot succeed without a verified signal.
claims.quote: there is no `verified` flag to forget to gate on. Success outputs: `wallet`, `conviction`, `action`, `window`, `signer`, `issuedAt`, `ageSeconds`.
claims.reasoning: The success ReadSignalResult type contains wallet, conviction, action, window, signer, issuedAt, ageSeconds — no verified field — and success: true is only reached after the verification guard at line 955.

claims.text: A 429 or a 5xx response is attributed as EXTERNAL.
claims.quote: a 429 and a 5xx are `EXTERNAL`
claims.reasoning: 429 is explicitly handled with errorClass: EXTERNAL; the catch-all for non-ok responses uses status >= 500 ? EXTERNAL : USER, attributing all 5xx as EXTERNAL.

claims.text: A 404, a 402, or an unparseable PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL is attributed as USER.
claims.quote: a 404, a 402 and an unparseable `PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL` are `USER`
claims.reasoning: Unparseable URL returns USER before assertUrlIsPublic is called; 404 and 402 status responses both return USER errorClass.

claims.text: A body that is not a Predge response is attributed as EXTERNAL unless the operator repointed the host.
claims.quote: a body that is not a Predge response is `EXTERNAL` unless the operator repointed the host
claims.reasoning: blameForBadBody returns USER when credentials.PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL is set (operator repointed host) and EXTERNAL otherwise; it is called for all bad-body cases.

claims.text: The default pin is a source constant in predge-core.ts equal to the attestation-role key published at https://api.predge.io/.well-known/predge-keys.json.
claims.quote: The default pin is a source constant in `predge-core.ts`, equal to the `attestation`-role key published at `https://api.predge.io/.well-known/predge-keys.json`.
claims.reasoning: DEFAULT_PINNED_SIGNER is a source constant in predge-core.ts; the comment links it to the attestation-role key at the published URL. The reviewer (suisuss, review[6]) independently confirmed the hex value is byte-identical to the live published key.

claims.text: Nothing reads the keyset at run time.
claims.quote: Nothing reads the keyset at run time
claims.reasoning: predge-core.ts uses a hardcoded DEFAULT_PINNED_SIGNER for offline verification and never fetches the keyset; only testPredge in test.ts fetches /.well-known/predge-keys.json, and only for connection-test purposes.

claims.text: PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID lets an operator override the pinned key ahead of a rotation, as noted in credentials.ts.
claims.quote: `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` lets an operator move ahead of one, as noted in `credentials.ts`.
claims.reasoning: credentials.ts documents PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID under a 'Rotation path' comment that explicitly says operators can set it to the new published key to move ahead of a plugin release.

claims.text: parseConvictionPayload runs after verification in the step and fails unless conviction is a finite number in 0–100, action is one of accumulate/reduce/hold, and window is one of 7d/30d, with no coercion.

claims.text: parseMaxAgeSeconds honours the value 0 literally, so an operator setting 0 rejects every signal rather than silently falling back to the default.
claims.quote: `parseMaxAgeSeconds` now honours `0`
claims.reasoning: parseMaxAgeSeconds returns 0 when raw is '0' because '0'.trim() is truthy and Number('0')=0 passes the isFinite and >= 0 checks; maxAgeSeconds=0 means ageMs > 0 rejects every positive-age signal.

claims.text: resource is declared on PredgeAttestation and covered by the signature.

claims.reasoning: PredgeAttestation has resource: string; canonicalize serializes all Object.keys() of the attestation including resource; canonical bytes are what the signature is verified over.

claims.quote: six ordered checks with `resource` fifth
claims.reasoning: Code order: scheme (528), signer (531), signature (536), subject binding (543), resource binding (550), freshness (564/567) — resource is exactly fifth.
claims.maintainer: six ordered checks with resource fifth

claims.text: The 64 KiB cap is enforced by content-length header first, then by the body length.
claims.quote: the 64 KiB cap checked by header and then by length
claims.reasoning: content-length header is read and checked against MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES before response.text(); body.length is checked after response.text() and before JSON.parse().

claims.text: Error attribution is conditional: failures on the default host are EXTERNAL; failures caused by operator-set PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID or PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL are USER.
claims.quote: Blaming the operator only when they set `PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID` or `PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL` … on the defaults those failures are the upstream's
claims.reasoning: classifyVerificationFailure returns USER only when the operator set PREDGE_SIGNER_KEY_ID or PREDGE_SIGNAL_URL (via blameForBadBody); all other verification failures default to EXTERNAL.
